This reveals two properties: most candidates barely shift the probed distribution, and both successful and failed source actions can be reinforced or suppressed. These observations motivate Anchor, which tests shift magnitude and source-role alignment before retention. Admitted memories guide later trajectories, enabling experience-driven improvement under a frozen policy. On held-out ALFWorld and WebShop tasks, Anchor improves success rate and mean score by up to 19.9% and 17.2%, respectively, relative to the strongest baseline for each backbone.   <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  A causal video generator writes every segment it produces into a key--value (KV) cache, and later segments know the past only through it. We find that writing and generating are different roles: in a pretrained generator the written KV already differs from the KV used for denoising, and on shared weights the gradient from future reads is negatively aligned with the gradient of generation. We propose dKV Forcing (dKV denotes differentiable KV), which gives the write its own parameters, a low-rank residual used only when a segment enters the cache, and trains them with the gradient of the later segments that read what they wrote. Opening this gradient through the cache in common use exhausts GPU memory. We trace this to checkpoint replay re-writing the cache, not to the gradient path, which removes the need for the second reconstruction pass of SGF. dKV Forcing keeps the cache as persistent differentiable pages and computes the exact gradient in one temporal traversal, with an $11\%$ lower memory peak and $28\%$ less resident memory. With pages that store hidden states, it trains 15\,s clips on which the two-pass reconstruction runs out of memory. Trained on 5\,s clips, dKV Forcing reaches the highest VBench-Long quality score at 60\,s and 240\,s and outperforms SGF by $3.6$ and $6.1$ points of aesthetic quality, with a higher dynamic degree.
  </details>

  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Large vision-language models (LVLMs) can be efficiently customized by fine-tuning only a lightweight connector, but this fine-tuning stage also exposes them to backdoor attacks. To counteract this threat, existing defenses inspect the behavior or the attention of the released model. However, they mostly inspect the model with all visual tokens, implicitly assuming that the deployed model sees the same tokens, which rarely holds since visual-token compression is widely adopted to reduce inference cost. In this paper, we find that compression can hide a dormant backdoor attack from inspection and awaken it during deployment, as the redundant tokens regulate the strength of the trigger. Specifically, without compression, the trigger is diluted by the redundant tokens around it, whereas compression keeps the trigger for its high importance and discards its context, a phenomenon we term context stripping. Inspired by this finding, we propose StripWake, a compressor-agnostic backdoor attack whose trigger takes effect only under compression. StripWake (i) poisons each training image in four views (clean or triggered, with all or compressed tokens) and asks for the target only in the compressed triggered view, and (ii) aligns the attention on clean compressed views with a frozen benign teacher to preserve clean utility. Extensive experiments show that StripWake stays dormant with all visual tokens and reliably wakes up under compression while preserving clean utility, is far more robust to existing defenses than published backdoor attacks, and generalizes to different architectures, model sizes and compressors unseen in training.
  </details>

We study this problem using videos of ongoing activities and forecast future activities through a named-concept state.   <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Spatial reasoning in Vision-Language Models (VLMs) has increasingly benefited from tool-integrated pipelines that ground computation in explicit geometry. However, existing systems often compile queries into relatively open-ended artifacts, such as code, task constraints, tool plans, or gathered evidence, leaving what must be resolved before execution under-specified. This can lead to unnecessary tool acquisition and iterative refinement, while still producing plausible reasoning traces from incomplete spatial commitments. We identify this failure mode as under-committed query compilation. To address it, we propose PEPS, a training-free agent Parsing Executable Primitives for Spatial reasoning under a typed FESM schema over Frame, Entity, State, and Metric. PEPS follows a parse-before-execute principle: the Parser commits each query to a compact set of executable requirements; the Executor selectively grounds the required primitives through fixed geometric APIs and deterministic computation; and the Verifier checks whether these requirements are fulfilled, enabling early termination or targeted repair. Experiments on three spatial reasoning benchmarks and four VLM backbones show that PEPS improves reasoning accuracy while substantially reducing refinement rounds, API cost, and end-to-end latency over strong tool-integrated baselines. These results demonstrate that knowing what a query requires before execution makes tool-integrated spatial reasoning not only more reliable, but also more efficient.
  </details>

  _Yuanbo Lyu, Changjian Pan, Saining Zhang, Yi Yang, Peishuo Li, Zhiheng Li, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  High-quality articulated assets are essential for embodied perception, simulation, and manipulation, yet constructing them at scale remains difficult. Manual annotation and procedural modeling require substantial human effort. Recent agentic systems automate asset construction through program synthesis, but repeat costly reasoning and refinement for every new asset. Our key observation is that assets within a category can share construction logic despite variations in structure and appearance. Agentic synthesis and procedural generation are therefore complementary: agents can construct reusable programs, while procedural execution reuses the resulting logic across many samples. We therefore present RFW-A, which combines the two in a new articulated-asset generation paradigm. Starting from existing articulated programs, RFW-A organizes reusable components and their dependencies into category-level generators. Agents test and refine these generators across sampled configurations and motion states. Once constructed and validated, the generators produce diverse assets through procedural execution with no further model calls or token charges. The estimated API cost of generator authoring averages $10.62, amortizing to $0.05 per asset over 200 assets, versus $1.24 for the sampled per-asset agentic synthesis baseline. Using RFW-A, we built RFW-A-400K, containing over 400K sim-ready articulated assets across more than 500 categories. Experiments show high structural and kinematic validity and stable execution across physics simulators. Beyond asset validity, training with RFW-A-400K improves part-level articulation estimation on seen and unseen categories, while policies trained in simulation with retrieved and program-edited assets transfer zero-shot to real articulated objects.

  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>

LabWorld recovers reusable 3D assets, a metric scene, time-varying object states, and procedure events. Multi-frame observations provide complementary evidence for asset and scene reconstruction, while motion reconstruction combines visual and geometric observations with event constraints encoding the spatial and temporal requirements of laboratory interactions. We evaluate LabWorld on real pipetting and vortexing videos collected in our laboratory against general-purpose agentic and dedicated reconstruction baselines. For pipetting, LabWorld achieves a mean Mask IoU of 0.501, exceeding the strongest baseline by 0.033. We integrate the tangent over the analytically known remaining VP angle to obtain a nominal one-step transport, and use the endpoint displacement to correct its long-horizon extrapolation through a constrained projection. This transport-first, correction-second construction yields Endpoint-Calibrated Transport (ECT), a closed-form, training-free editor requiring only one noise level, two text conditions packed into one denoiser batch, and one latent update.   </details>

  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>

Conditioned on the partially generated sample and the generator's features, our policy chooses which positions to fill next and/or which previously filled positions to mask for later regeneration, a mechanism we call rethinking. For the latter, we introduce FIDgrad, an image-level reward derived from the (first-order) change in Fréchet Inception Distance caused by adding a generated sample to the current feature distribution. We compare CryoTracer with five reference methods on EMPIAR-10022 and a private, in-house $\alpha$-synuclein collection. The standard regime uses the full training partition, while the practical regime limits training to 50 annotated micrographs. A separate $\alpha$-synuclein split tests transfer to held-out sessions. CryoTracer achieves the highest complete-filament mF1, continuous coverage, and crossing accuracy among the evaluated methods in both regimes. We release new filament centerline annotations for EMPIAR-10022. Code and data are available atthis https URL
  </details>

- **[Find the Fungible: Variable-Resolution Tokenization that Compacts Semantics with a Granularity Dial as a VLM "Catalyst"](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18690)**  `arXiv:2610.18690`  
  _Tianhao Fu, Austin Wang, Charles Chen, Roby Aldave-Garza, Victor Xie_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Efficient vision-language models should preserve a useful representation of the whole image, even under tight budgets. However, aggressive pruning or indiscriminate merging can erase critical details and disrupt the spatial structure. We thus propose Varest, which maximizes semantic fungibility: tokens describing coherent content can be summarized together with minimal information loss. Object boundaries distilled from a visual foundation model guide grouping, while text localization protects details needed for reading. At lower budgets, Varest merges the image into coarser semantic regions, while maintaining full spatial coverage. After early language decoder layers process this representation, a learned selector prunes visual tokens that later layers no longer need, reducing repeated access to already integrated information. Across three LLaVA backbones and 13 benchmarks, Varest outperforms 10 training-free and 5 trained baselines in mean performance retention at every evaluated budget, preserving 86.10-92.33% of uncompressed performance using only 5.56% of tokens. This SOTA performance further generalizes to modern VLMs like Qwen3.8-27B.
  </details>

- **[Urbex: Agentic Spatial Grounding for City-Scale 3D Scenes](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.18356)**  `arXiv:2610.18356`  
  _Yu Wang, Rui Dai, Wei Chen, Yi Wang, Bo Dang, Kaikui Liu, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  City-scale 3D grounding is commonly formulated as candidate ranking, which requires precomputed instance proposals and becomes inefficient in large outdoor scenes. We propose Urbex, an agentic vision-language framework that instead casts grounding as active spatial search. Urbex represents a city-scale 3D scene as an interactive multi-view environment, allowing a VLM agent to query landmarks, zoom into local regions, render oblique views, and commit a grounded bounding box. We optimize this tool-use policy with reinforcement learning on CityRefer, using smooth localization rewards and lightweight shaping rewards for efficient exploration. Experiments show that Urbex achieves the best Hit@1 and IoU on CityRefer, supports candidate-free grounding without ground-truth boxes, and is substantially faster than the strongest city-scale ranking baseline. Zero-shot results on STPLS3D-Refer further indicate improved cross-scene robustness.
  </details>

- **[Image Diffusion Models Are Good 3D Human Motion Generators](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.14254)**  `arXiv:2610.14254`  
  _Siyuan Yang, Chong Wang, Hao Cheng, Jun Liu, Bihan Wen, Alex Kot, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Text-to-motion generation typically relies on dataset-specific skeletal representations, with models trained separately for benchmarks with different joint layouts. We investigate whether image diffusion architectures can model 3D human motion through a common image-compatible representation that accommodates heterogeneous skeletal layouts while preserving motion-specific kinematic structure. To this end, we organize root-centered joint trajectories into topology-informed joint--time images and model global root dynamics through a complementary latent stream. A motion autoencoder conditions local-motion decoding on the root latent, while a text-conditioned Scalable Interpolant Transformer (SiT) jointly generates both latent streams, with supervision on decoded 3D joint positions further constraining generation in motion space. In addition to dataset-specific models, we train a single motion autoencoder on HumanML3D and KIT-ML, followed by a single text-conditioned SiT shared across both datasets, preserving their respective skeletal definitions without skeleton retargeting to a common joint layout. Experiments on HumanML3D and KIT-ML show that our dataset-specific models achieve state-of-the-art performance, while shared training yields further gains on both benchmarks, demonstrating the benefits of shared modeling across heterogeneous skeletal layouts.
  </details>

- **[Seek-and-View Reasoning for Multi-View Spatial Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.11810)**  `arXiv:2610.11810`  
  _Qixiang Chen, Cheng Zhang, Fucai Ke, Chi-Wing Fu, Jianfei Cai, Jingwen Ye_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Existing multi-view spatial reasoning remains constrained by sparse and fixed viewpoints. Consequently, vision-language models (VLMs) must infer spatial relations solely from these fixed views, leading to fragile cross-view alignment and a geometry-to-language bottleneck. To overcome these issues, we formulate a novel Seek-and-View reasoning paradigm that seeks a viewpoint to make the queried spatial relation directly observable and interprets the sought view to support the spatial reasoning. Building on this paradigm, we propose Vantage, a training-free and model-agnostic framework that structures VLM reasoning for viewpoint planning and evidence-augmented spatial understanding, with a 3D foundation model supporting view synthesis. Specifically, we develop a viewpoint-grounded reasoning stage that translates spatial queries into targeted viewpoint plans. A subsequent geometry-grounded evidence augmentation stage synthesizes new views and incorporates visual evidence alongside preceding reasoning contexts for final answering. Together, these stages reduce reliance on language-based cross-view alignment. Extensive experiments on six VLMs across six benchmarks show consistent improvements in overall accuracy, with an average absolute gain of 8.2% without fine-tuning.
  </details>

- **[GS-Pool: Object-Level Change Detection in 3D Gaussian Splatting](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06688)**  `arXiv:2610.06688`  
  _Boaz Keren-Gil, James Gain, Patrick Marais_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Many physical spaces require photographic monitoring of changes to their structure over time. When each visit is reconstructed with 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), a direct comparison of the two reconstructions cannot answer this because training is stochastic and two reconstructions of an unchanged space never coincide. To address this, we propose GS-Pool, which takes two independently reconstructed Gaussian scans of the same space and returns the changed objects in each, together with their change masks. Our method begins by extracting SAM2 masks from the photographs of each visit. These are then lifted onto the Gaussians that render them and merged into an object pool, a collection of 3D objects, so every decision is taken once per object in 3D. We introduce a novel photographic carrier approach, which co-opts the existing 3DGS mechanism. It does so by applying the photographs of the other visit and back-propagating them to the Gaussians that rendered each pixel. We combine this with GS-Diff's geometry and colour terms and our distilled DINOv3 features. This evidence is compared with objects identified as unchanged in both visits to set a change threshold for each scene. On the PASLCD benchmark, GS-Pool achieves mIoU/F1 scores of 0.75/0.85 against 0.64/0.76 for GS-Diff, the strongest offline method for detecting change in 3DGS. Finally, we return each changed object as a set of Gaussians, which can be inspected in 3D.
  </details>

- **[Bayesian Optimization in Sequence-to-Architecture Latent Space for Zero-Shot NAS](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.06167)**  `arXiv:2610.06167`  
  _Ondrej Tybl, Lukas Neumann_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Zero-shot Neural Architecture Search removes the prohibitive cost of traditional NAS, but its search process is typically based on the evolutionary algorithm (EA); lacking an explicit model of the objective, it often resorts to a near-random search through mutation. Bayesian Optimization offers a principled alternative by modeling the objective and aggregating information across iterations, but scales poorly to the high-dimensional, discrete, graph-structured spaces of modern NAS, restricting its use to only small networks. In this paper, we bring Bayesian Optimization to zero-shot NAS for large-scale architectures by learning a latent space via a Variational Autoencoder trained to reconstruct a novel prefix encoding of architectures and propose a proxy scalarization that combines several zero-shot proxies into a single Bayesian Optimization objective. After only 10,000 iterations of the proposed search algorithm (8 hours on a single GPU), our method found a network architecture which under the given model parameter count constraints achieves state-of-the-art results on three separate tasks -- image classification, object detection and semantic segmentation.
  </details>

- **[Motion Without State: Probing Dynamical Consistency and Conditioning Bias in Video Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.05135)**  `arXiv:2610.05135`  
  _Weihan Li, Junhao Wu, Yuhan Song, Xiaofeng Lin, Xinlei Chen_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Image-to-video models serve as visual world priors whose plausible motion departs from physical simulation. We ask what dynamical structure replaces forward state propagation in generated motion, and how it biases quantitative physics evaluation. Holding law and initial state fixed, we vary visible geometry, prompt wording, and clip length across nine models and compare tracked trajectories against simulator rollouts. Generated motion splits into local visual cues and global boundary control, omitting the propagating physical state between them. Locally, tempo-normalized speed follows track undulations with a 15°-41° phase lead toward steepest descent as mean slope barely accelerates the ball, showing short memory of past slope. Local responses fail to compose: no single contact law describes a model's bounces (prescribed, self-calibrated on single-deflector contacts, or fitted in-sample), and balls clear 43 of 49 barriers above release height under an outcome-free prompt. Globally, naming the catch tray lifts arrival 14-76 percentage points above post-contact simulator rollouts, and event duration scales near-linearly with clip length, making apparent gravity 5.6-7.3 times higher in 3 s than in 8 s clips. These patterns persist on photographed first frames, motivating neutral-prompt controls, exit-state rollouts, and tempo-normalized metrics.
  </details>

- **[Where to Look Is Not How to Fix: Pre-Denoising Diagnostics and Modality-Dependent Control in Diffusion Composition](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.03068)**  `arXiv:2610.03068`  
  _Fangzheng Wu, Brian Summa_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Understanding compositional failures in text-to-image diffusion requires identifying both where stress is detectable and how intervention changes the output. We study these questions through a controlled anchor--stress protocol that jointly evaluates text-encoder diagnostics and denoiser interventions. We introduce a text-only Compositional Stress Index (CSI), which separates common from rare compositions across SD1.5, SDXL, and the SD3 text path and provides an upstream diagnostic coordinate. A matched six-prompt localization study links intervention location to distinct outcomes: residual-minimizing embedding adapters improve representation fit, while downstream cross-attention intervention increases color hit rate (CHR) by 0.0272. Across SD1.5 and SDXL denoiser blocks, the largest positive signed diagnostic-accessibility mean occurs at the deep encoder, whereas selective boost has its largest positive mean CHR response at decoder blocks. Selective subtraction and broad ablation reveal further modality- and architecture-dependent responses, including a substantial CHR decrease when SDXL decoder cross-attention is broadly ablated. We find a diagnosis-control dissociation under our controlled attribute-object composition setting: compositional defects are diagnosable before denoising, but the representation coordinate that exposes risk is not necessarily the coordinate or modality that improves generation.
  </details>

- **[Learning via Self-Consistency for Diffusion-based Video Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36826)**  `arXiv:2609.36826`  
  _Zhenghao Ni, Weimin Qiu, Meng Tang_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  While video diffusion models have demonstrated emerging zero-shot capability for visual reasoning and perception tasks, their stochastic generations often produce inconsistent predictions for tasks requiring reliable, structured outputs. Prior work has shown that self-consistency across stochastic video generations can improve diffusion-based reasoning at test time. We systematically extend the test-time method to structured prediction problems such as referring segmentation. However, test time scaling via self-consistency requires multiple rollouts and incurs much more latency. We propose self-consistency as an intrinsic learning signal for post-training video diffusion models without ground truth annotations or external verifiers. Specifically, our proposed Self-Consistency Fine-Tuning (SC-FT) distills consensus predictions into the video generation model, while subsequent Self-Consistency Reinforcement Learning (SC-RL) rewards generations according to their agreement with the consensus. The resulting model effectively internalizes the benefit of multi-sample consensus and requires only a single generation at inference time, while substantially outperforming the original model. To further reduce inference overhead, we read out predictions early in the denoising trajectory, preserving consensus quality while cutting inference time per rollout by 52%. For visual search, our method raises task accuracy from 48.4% for a single generation to 99.1%. For maze solving across three layout sizes, SC-FT and SC-RL improve single generation strict validity from 59.1% to 66.1% and 95.6% with the same inference latency. Also, for referring segmentation, SC-RL raises single-generation gIoU from 0.402 to 0.582, beyond SC-FT 0.473.
  </details>

- **[Sparse-View Interpretable 3D Animal Behavior Representations for Neural Encoding and Decoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.36217)**  `arXiv:2609.36217`  
  _Xinming Dai, Qihang Jin, Jiaying Zhang, Tianshu Tan, Baiyuan Chen, Hanrui Lyu, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  A deeper understanding of brain function requires a precise, structured characterization of behavior. Yet, extracting behavioral representations from video in a form suitable for scientific analysis remains a fundamental challenge. Many prior studies represent behavior via pose estimation or nonlinear video embeddings. However, pose tracking discards rich information beyond predefined keypoints, while nonlinear video embeddings lack interpretability. We address this limitation with SABLE (Sparse-view Animal Behavior Latent Embeddings), a self-supervised framework that leverages a geometric inductive bias to learn behavior representations. By augmenting a multi-view transformer with priors from monocular depth and pose estimation, SABLE reconstructs 3D animal behavior from extremely sparse views while learning explicit 3D latent structure. Without ground-truth 3D labels, it reliably recovers 3D behavior from two-view videos, whereas state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods fail or yield degenerate solutions. Across the International Brain Lab and Cheese3D datasets, we demonstrate that SABLE learns 3D representations that match or exceed prior SOTA performance in neural encoding and decoding. Single-neuron analyses further identify neurons with putative 3D tuning, generating testable hypotheses about how the brain represents 3D behavior. Once pretrained across animals, SABLE serves as an off-the-shelf model that generalizes zero-shot to unseen animals without animal-specific calibration or retraining. Our method establishes 3D-aware video embeddings that capture complex behavior, opening new avenues for studying brain-behavior relationships.
  </details>

- **[DirectUV: Image-Conditioned UV Texture Generation with Surface-Aware Positional Encoding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.34651)**  `arXiv:2609.34651`  
  _Jiantao Lin, Yingjie Xu, Mingzhi Sheng, Yangkai Wei, Hao Chen, Ying-Cong Chen_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Generating high-quality UV textures for 3D meshes remains challenging. Multi-view projection pipelines suffer from occlusion and view inconsistency, and recent methods that generate textures directly in UV space still rely on auxiliary modules to supply 3D information, leaving the attention mechanism tied to UV-grid positions rather than to the underlying surface geometry. This mismatch limits coherence across seams and disconnected UV islands.We propose DirectUV, an image-conditioned UV texture diffusion framework that operates in the latent UV space of a pretrained image VAE, in which a Diffusion Transformer denoises the UV latent given a single input image and a coarse UV map. At its core, Surface-Aware Positional Encoding (SAPE) replaces the standard 2D-grid positional encoding with encodings derived from per-token 3D surface coordinates obtained via UV-to-surface correspondence. As positional encodings define the distance metric used by attention, SAPE enables tokens to interact according to 3D positional proximity derived from surface correspondence rather than UV-grid distance, restoring coherence across seams and disconnected islands. A multi-level extension further assigns different attention heads to progressively finer subdivisions of the same latent UV patch, allowing the model to reason about surface structure at multiple granularities.Experiments show that DirectUV produces sharper and more globally consistent textures than other baselines, with the largest improvements in occluded and view-unseen regions where projection-based methods leave gaps or stretched textures.
  </details>

- **[Resolving State-Representation Mismatch: State-Space Visual Reasoning for Open-Loop VLA Planning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.33412)**  `arXiv:2609.33412`  
  _Junhao Xiao, Haoxiang Zhao, Menghao Fang, Jinkui Zhang, Jinghan Yu, Xinyu Huang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Despite rapid progress in vision-language-action (VLA) models, existing reasoning paradigms still face a fundamental \emph{state-representation mismatch} in open-loop planning. Given only an initial observation, models must internally simulate action-conditioned state transitions, whereas text-, pixel-, and latent-space reasoning can suffer from lossy spatial compression, error-accumulating visual generation, and bypass of intermediate latent tokens, respectively, undermining reliable long-horizon planning. We propose \textbf{State-Space Visual Reasoning} (SSVR), which decouples static visual context, language constraints, and a recurrent latent state. SSVR encodes the initial image and instruction once, then conditions each action prediction on the latent state and updates it with an action-conditioned GRU. Using Qwen2.5-VL as the backbone, SSVR achieves 99.5/99.6, 96.3/98.0, and 83.9/90.6 EM/PR on FrozenLake, Maze, and MiniBehavior, substantially outperforming prior methods. Extensive experiments support the effectiveness of recurrent state modeling for VLA open-loop planning across input transformations and transfer settings. By reusing static visual-textual context and updating a compact recurrent state, SSVR supports efficient multi-step inference, achieving up to $98.58\times$ faster Maze decoding rollouts than the evaluated baselines with the prefix cache prebuilt.
  </details>

- **[Forensic Twins: Self-Supervised Residual Learning for AI-Generated Image Forensics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.31514)**  `arXiv:2609.31514`  
  _Javier Muñoz-Haro, Ruben Tolosana, Ruben Vera-Rodriguez, Aythami Morales, Julian Fierrez_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Detectors of AI-generated images are typically trained using samples from specific Generative AI architectures and degrade as soon as a new architecture emerges. Recent approaches have explored self-supervised pre-training as an alternative solution, yet standard frameworks work against the forensic task, since their augmentations overwrite the micro-statistics of image formation. This paper introduces Forensic Twins, a Self-Supervised Residual Learning (SSRL) framework whose pretext task removes shared image content between views. Each image is mapped through a forensic residual extractor, from which two spatially disjoint crops are drawn. Sharing no pixel, the two views leave the redundancy-reduction objective with a predominantly content-independent common signal, the stationary fingerprint of the image acquisition pipeline. The encoder is exclusively trained on real images; no AI-generated image is used to learn the representation. Experiments show competitive results in zero-shot, few-shot, and linear probing scenarios, reaching 97.21% AUC across 26 unseen AI generators, including GANs, diffusion models, and commercial systems. We also provide insightful analysis on the learned representation regarding unsupervised clustering on different AI generators and its forensic properties. Code, weights and exact splits are publicly available.
  </details>

- **[ConsistWorld: Evidence Routing for Consistent Multi-Agent World Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.22641)**  `arXiv:2609.22641`  
  _Qianxun Xu, Xianfang Zeng, Xinyao Liao, Wei Cheng, Gang Yu, Chi Zhang_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Autoregressive video world models enable temporally coherent generation for a single observer. Extending them to multiple agents requires consistency across independently controlled views and temporal gaps under causal streaming. We present ConsistWorld, a multi-agent world model that generates camera-controlled video streams of a static scene from one shared image. We formulate consistency as routing evidence from committed multi-agent history and concurrently generated peer views to the tokens being generated. Pose Conditioned Memory Retrieval selects relevant historical observations from all agents, recovering evidence beyond the recent context window. Visibility-Gated Peer Sharing regulates current peer information according to estimated historical coverage and current-view overlap. Together, they determine which historical observations enter the context and where concurrent peer information contributes, supporting long-term recall and coordinated exploration. Both mechanisms use camera geometry and maintain a bounded active context for a fixed agent count and retrieval budget. Experiments on evidence sharing cases and video length and agent number generalizations show that ConsistWorld achieves a strong cross-time and cross-agent consistency while preserving competitive generation quality.
  </details>

- **[PointEvent: Polarity-Conditioned Motion Evidence Accumulation for Event-Based Tiny Object Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.20066)**  `arXiv:2609.20066`  
  _Zongze Wu, Baofeng Jia, Weiqi Yan, Jingyuan Zhang, Min Liu, Yu Zang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Event cameras offer high temporal resolution and motion sensitivity for tiny UAV detection, but distant targets produce sparse, fragmented events easily overwhelmed by clutter and noise. Dense aggregation mixes weak target responses with background activity, while local spatiotemporal modeling may fail to connect distant observations. Polarity encodes the sign of brightness change; a moving target tends to produce opposite polarities at its leading and trailing boundaries, whose spatial arrangement indicates motion direction. We propose PointEvent, which serializes events into complementary spatiotemporal and timestamp orders. Spatiotemporal orders preserve x-y-t locality, while timestamp orders preserve temporal succession across spatial neighborhoods, establishing long-range propagation paths. Along each path, a recurrent state accumulates evidence, while polarity routes each event to its corresponding state subspace. This separates how evidence propagates from where it is written. Experiments on EV-UAV and ES-UAV demonstrate state-of-the-art accuracy with the fewest parameters (0.12M) and fastest measured inference (29.9 ms) among compared methods. Code:this https URL
  </details>

- **[EgoPathBench: Evaluating Zero-Shot Egocentric Waypoint Decision-Making in Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.16610)**  `arXiv:2609.16610`  
  _Yang Zhao, Zhuo Chen, Xubo Yang_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Widely used spatial-QA benchmarks increasingly motivate embodied navigation, yet evaluate foundation vision-language models (VLMs) through isolated queries about space rather than feasible action sequences in space. However, zero-shot waypoint navigation requires turning spatial understanding into a feasible action sequence: from a single first-person view, a model must jointly ground the target, respect agent-specific clearance, maintain edge-by-edge legality, and stop at the goal. To evaluate this capability, we introduce EgoPathBench, a dataset and five-task benchmark for first-person waypoint decision-making. Each example pairs an egocentric RGB image, a natural-language goal, and numbered visible waypoints, and scores predicted candidate sets or ordered routes against registered 3D scene geometry under task-specific Point or Embodied feasibility graphs. EgoPathBench comprises 31,852 training, 1,345 validation, and 1,111 benchmark questions, with at least one verified reference route for every route question. Across ten foundation VLMs, the highest EgoPath Score is only 35.6. While models often make locally plausible choices and the top model reaches 41.7% success on Point Path, it drops to 10.0% on both Embodied Path and Intent Path, with the remaining nine models below 3% on Embodied Path (and at most 4.0% on Intent Path) -- exposing a sharp gap between local plausibility and complete embodied routes. Beyond evaluation, we construct the EgoPath-SFT training set. Fine-tuning Qwen3.5-4B on EgoPath-SFT raises its EgoPath Score from 3.9 to 38.9, improves closed-loop Isaac Sim execution by 20 percentage points, and transfers consistently to three external spatial benchmarks.
  </details>

- **[SignSeek: Learning Transferable Representations for Sign Dictionary Retrieval](https://arxiv.org/abs/2609.03695)**  `arXiv:2609.03695`  
  _Sobhan Asasi, Ozge Mercanoglu Sincan, Richard Bowden_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Sign language dictionaries are essential resources for sign language learners, yet automatically retrieving a sign from a dictionary, given only a query video, remains a challenging problem due to the natural variability between signers. Existing sign representation learning methods are built for closed-set recognition, producing embeddings that do not generalise to the open-set, signer-independent setting that retrieval demands. \textbf{SignSeek} closes this gap by contrastively learning sign representations with saliency-guided articulator masking. A contrastive objective aligns same-gloss signs across signers, while our Articulator Saliency-Guided Masking (ASGM) pinpoints the single most critical articulator per sign. This drives two complementary objectives, a masked contrastive alignment (MAC) loss that sees the sign through a single articulator and a masked prediction (MAP) loss that reconstructs it in latent space from the surrounding spatio-temporal context. Pretrained on 266K samples ($\sim$5,700 glosses) across multiple sign languages, \textbf{SignSeek} sets a new state-of-the-art performance in cross-corpus retrieval on ASL-Citizen, WLASL, and NMFs-CSL without any downstream fine-tuning. Strikingly, it achieves zero-shot generalisation to an entirely unseen British Sign Language (BSL), surpassing methods explicitly trained on BSL, and transfers seamlessly to isolated sign recognition and subtitle alignment, outperforming prior skeleton-based methods.
  </details>

- **[GraspHOI: Full-Body 3D Human-Object Reconstruction with Articulated Hands from a Single In-the-Wild Image](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.28386)**  `arXiv:2608.28386`  
  _Semin Kim, Haechan Shin, Jongyoo Kim_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Existing monocular full-body 3D human-object interaction (HOI) methods do not combine category-agnostic object reconstruction with finger-level contact. Their hands may float off or sink into objects, breaking realism in AR/VR environments. We present GraspHOI, the first category-agnostic framework that reconstructs a full-body 3D HOI from a single image and jointly refines the arms and fingers so that the hands meet the reconstructed object surface. GraspHOI reconstructs the body, hands, and object separately with foundation models and places them in a shared metric camera frame through depth-based registration and silhouette alignment. Occlusion-aware contact correspondences seat the object against the hand, and contact-aware optimization refines shoulder, elbow, wrist, and finger rotations while anchoring the joints to the image. We find that with fingers capped near the image estimate, refining them alone is insufficient; freeing the arm removes most of the remaining hand-object gap, since in a full body the arm chain places the hand. In experiments on three datasets, GraspHOI yields more plausible hand-object contact than four baselines and better relative human-object placement than HDM and TeHOR.
  </details>

- **[ArmorOCR: Grounded Adversarial Visual Perception via Observation-Transferred Self-Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.20122)**  `arXiv:2608.20122`  
  _Linhan Cao, Siyuan Li, Jun Lan, Liangbo He, Guannan Li, Xiaolei Huang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Large multimodal models (LMMs) have demonstrated strong OCR recognition capabilities, yet remain vulnerable to adversarial visual text that is readable to humans but challenging for models to localize and recognize. Existing OCR benchmarks mainly focus on natural or document-style text, while adversarial OCR evaluations remain limited in scale, task coverage, or region-aware evaluation. In this paper, we formulate adversarial OCR as a \textbf{grounded OCR perception} task and introduce \textbf{AdvSpot}, the first benchmark for grounded adversarial OCR evaluation. AdvSpot comprises 383 images with region-level annotations, spanning 5 primary categories and 13 fine-grained adversarial OCR types. To address this challenge, we propose \textbf{ArmorOCR}, a two-stage training framework for robust adversarial OCR perception. ArmorOCR first acquires missing adversarial OCR perception from privileged transformed observations through On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD), and then refines grounded OCR perception through Group Relative Policy Optimization (GRPO) with task-conditioned rewards for localization, recognition, full spotting, and visual question answering (VQA). Experiments on our AdvSpot, other adversarial OCR benchmarks, and general OCR benchmarks demonstrate that ArmorOCR consistently improves adversarial OCR perception while preserving competitive general OCR capability. The benchmark and code are available atthis https URL
  </details>

- **[AdaGEM: Granularity Adaptation and Geospatial Evidence Modulation for Ultra-High-Resolution Remote Sensing Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.15075)**  `arXiv:2608.15075`  
  _Kexin Ma, Jing Xiao, Bowen Xing, Liang Liao, Chia-Wen Lin_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Ultra-high-resolution (UHR) remote sensing imagery provides rich spatial details and extensive geographic coverage for Earth observation understanding. However, such imagery generates quadratically growing visual token sequences, where sparse task-critical evidence is easily overwhelmed by redundant and task-irrelevant tokens, leading to excessive computation and ineffective evidence preservation. Existing methods seek to balance computational efficiency and task effectiveness through selective multi-scale inspection or direct token pruning, yet often overlook task-dependent granularity requirements and struggle to distinguish sparse critical evidence from overwhelming visual redundancy. To address these challenges, we propose AdaGEM, a unified framework that jointly adapts visual granularity to task demands and modulates token selection to preserve essential geospatial evidence. Specifically, a Granularity Router predicts detail requirements and evidence scope from the query, then selects input resolution and token budget via a rule-based mapping. At the adapted granularity, a Geospatial Evidence Modulator selects complementary visual tokens to preserve critical evidence and spatial context while suppressing redundancy in homogeneous regions. Extensive experiments across diverse remote sensing benchmarks and multiple MLLM backbones demonstrate that AdaGEM consistently improves task performance over strong baselines and existing UHR methods while substantially reducing inference costs.
  </details>

- **[DistMoE: Private-data Rehearsal-free Routing in Mixture-of-Experts for Distributed Instruction Tuning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09907)**  `arXiv:2608.09907`  
  _Mainak Singha, Niccolò Biondi, Elisa Ricci, Subhankar Roy_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have shown strong multimodal instruction-following ability, but adapting them to diverse visual-language domains typically assumes centralized data access and costly joint training. This is restrictive when data is distributed across private, domain-specific, or permission-limited clients. To this end, we propose DistMoE, a mixture-of-experts (MoE) approach for distributed visual instruction tuning. In each layer of the language decoder it augments the public feedforward network (FFN) with a client-specific private FFN expert, with the goal to acquire domain-specific knowledge. However, independent expert training causes the private FFNs to learn representation of different scales and magnitudes, making merging the experts difficult. To reduce client-specific drift, we introduce a public-anchored expert composition stage that updates only routers and lightweight private projection adapters on a mix of local client data and public data, via an isotropic regularization loss, therefore making it cross-client rehearsal-free composition. During inference, DistMoE performs modular routing over public and private experts, enabling token-wise domain composition without explicit domain labels. Experiments across diverse visual-language benchmarks show that DistMoE enables flexible expert reuse, effective domain adaptation, and competitive performance while preserving modular control over client-specific knowledge.
  </details>

- **[Beyond Statistical Priors: Architecture-Agnostic Data-Free Knowledge Distillation via Unified Explicit Semantics](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.09287)**  `arXiv:2608.09287`  
  _Xuewan He, Tong Chu, Zihan Cheng, Yuchen Su, Qianxin Xia, Guoming Lu, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Data-Free Knowledge Distillation (DFKD) transfers knowledge from a pretrained teacher model to a compact student model by synthesizing semantically informative data, eliminating the need for access to the original training dataset. Existing DFKD methods rely heavily on architecture-specific statistical priors (e.g., Batch Normalization statistics) to guide data synthesis; however, such architecture-dependent priors are often absent in modern architectures such as Vision Transformers (ViTs), resulting in degraded semantic quality of the synthesized data and consequently catastrophic performance degradation. In this paper, we propose UniDFKD, a unified data-free knowledge distillation framework that replaces architecture-specific statistics with explicit, architecture-agnostic semantic priors. UniDFKD governs the entire synthesis-distillation pipeline along three dimensions: (1) Categorical Semantic Conditioning (CSC) defines what to synthesize by persistently modulating the generator with language-derived embeddings to capture semantic diversity; (2) Spatial Semantic Anchoring (SSA) regularizes where evidence belongs by anchoring the teacher's spatial attributions to a Gaussian prior; and (3) Spatial Semantic Distillation (SSD) controls how knowledge is transferred by explicitly aligning teacher-student spatial evidence alongside predictions. Extensive experiments across CNNs and ViTs demonstrate that UniDFKD sets a new state of the art. It outperforms the strongest baseline NAYER by average absolute margins of 17.23 and 24.49 in top-1 accuracy under homogeneous and heterogeneous settings, respectively.
  </details>

- **[Adaptation Circuits for Compute-Efficient Fine-Tuning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.08336)**  `arXiv:2608.08336`  
  _Uri Z. Kialy, Gil Ben-Artzi_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning (PEFT) has become the de facto standard for adapting Vision Transformers (ViTs) to downstream tasks. While parameter count has been the dominant efficiency metric in PEFT, it does not imply compute efficiency: parameter-sparse methods can still incur full-model training cost per step, and typically need long schedules to reach peak accuracy. Across seven fine-tuning methods on ViT-B/16, trainable parameters span $0.1\%$ to $100\%$ of the backbone, while the measured time of a training epoch stays within $0.74\times$ to $1.69\times$ that of full fine-tuning and does not necessarily grow with the trainable fraction. We introduce Circuit Fine-Tuning (CFT), which uses attribution to select an adaptation circuit, a parameter-budgeted set of attention heads and MLP blocks, before any task head is trained, and tunes it in place, reducing the number of training steps rather than the cost of a step. CFT adds no parameters, uses no learning-rate warmup, and leaves the inference graph unchanged. On VTAB-1k, CFT is comparable with the most accurate baseline while reaching its best checkpoint after $24$ epochs on average, against $35$ to $72$ for the baselines; at equal accuracy the most efficient baseline needs $1.1$ to $3.6\times$ the training FLOPs of CFT and $1.6$ to $3.8\times$ its training time. In a $5$-epoch comparison under domain shift, on mammography lesions (CBIS-DDSM), CFT has the highest F1 on ViT-B/16 and Swin-v2-B and ties on DINOv2. A feasibility study applies CFT to a vision-language model (Gemma-3) as well.
  </details>

- **[UniView: Large-Baseline View Synthesis via Video Diffusion Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.04701)**  `arXiv:2608.04701`  
  _Wangbo Yu, Haiyang Zhou, Chaoran Feng, Xunyu Zhou, Li Yuan_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Novel view synthesis from casually captured monocular images and videos offers a practical route to immersive content creation without dedicated multi-view capture. However, the limited viewpoint coverage of such inputs leaves scene geometry insufficiently constrained, restricting the ability of reconstruction-based methods, such as neural radiance fields (NeRF) and 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS), to render views far from the observed viewpoints. Generative approaches leverage learned visual priors to synthesize unobserved content, but maintaining geometric consistency and precise camera control remains challenging under large viewpoint changes. We present UniView, a unified framework for large-baseline novel view synthesis and scene generation from monocular images and videos. Central to our approach are an occlusion-aware point cloud renderer and a dual-branch conditioning mechanism. The renderer uses triple reprojection to identify and filter unreliable projections under large viewpoint changes. The conditioning mechanism integrates the resulting geometric guidance with source-view appearance within the video diffusion model, enabling precise camera control while preserving visual details and synthesizing unobserved content. To extend view synthesis to scene generation, we introduce a two-stage generation strategy that decouples viewpoint changes from temporal evolution. This strategy produces dense, synchronized multi-view videos that provide additional supervision for dynamic Gaussian Splatting, enabling more complete 4D generation from monocular observations. Extensive evaluations across static and dynamic scenes demonstrate the effectiveness of UniView in novel view synthesis and scene generation, combining precise camera control with geometric consistency and visual fidelity.
  </details>

- **[ISRS-DETR: Detection-Guided Click Propagation for Remote Sensing Interactive Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.02468)**  `arXiv:2608.02468`  
  _Thanh Duc Pham, Anh Nguyen, Duong Duc Hieu, Minh-Tan Pham_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Interactive segmentation reduces the prohibitive cost of pixel-level annotation by allowing users to delineate objects with a few clicks. However, applying this paradigm directly to remote sensing imagery is non-trivial: ultra-high resolutions, small object sizes, and sparse spatial distributions all degrade segmentation quality. Recent work has addressed the resolution barrier and achieved competitive results in interactive segmentation for remote sensing (ISRS). However, they treat all instances of a class within an image as a single objective target. Consequently, interactions spent on one object contribute nothing to its same-class neighbours, and satisfactory masks may hinder the practicality of these frameworks. We observe that remote sensing scenes exhibit markedly strong inter-object correlation, meaning a single clicked object is highly informative about the rest of its category. Building on this, we propose ISRS-DETR, a detection-guided interactive segmentation framework that injects object-level evidence into both training and inference. Our ISRS-DETR employs a looped DETR-based decoder, a single weight-shared decoder layer iterated several times, with the interactive segmentation backbone to localise co-occurring same-class objects, and introduces a Dynamic Top-K Click Selection strategy that retains only reliable proposals and converts each into a simulated click, so one user interaction propagates across an entire class. Experiments on three standard remote sensing benchmarks show that ISRS-DETR achieves state-of-the-art accuracy while substantially reducing Number of Clicks (NoC). Code will be released for reproducibility upon acceptance.
  </details>

- **[AeroLLE: Nighttime Aerial Image Enhancement with Generated Supervision](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00702)**  `arXiv:2608.00702`  
  _Wei Lu, Hongyuan Liu, Liuqian Wang, Qi Ming, Xue Yang, Si-Bao Chen_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Nighttime aerial image enhancement is constrained by the scarcity of aligned normal-light targets. Acquiring such targets from moving UAVs is difficult, and simple darkening of daytime images underrepresents the sensor noise, localized lighting, and uneven exposure of real nighttime captures. Generating normal-light references from real nighttime observations offers a practical way to fill this supervision gap. AeroNight pairs 1,200 real nighttime aerial RGB images with generated references selected through manual screening, preserving real imaging degradation in the inputs. This setting motivates AeroLLE, a lightweight two-stage framework whose context-aware Base Enhancer combines local processing with scene-level frequency information to recover visibility. Spatially Adaptive Exposure-Color Calibration (SAECC) then refines the base prediction through bounded low-resolution RGB gain and bias fields. AeroLLE achieves the highest PSNR and SSIM among the evaluated methods on both held-out test sets, reaching 17.62/17.89 dB PSNR and 0.5190/0.4964 SSIM on Test 1/Test 2, respectively. The model uses 255.24K parameters and 2.47G FLOPs, reducing FLOPs by 85.4\% relative to Multinex and improving PSNR by 1.56 dB on Test 2. AeroNight provides the first benchmark for pseudo-supervised nighttime aerial enhancement, and AeroLLE shows that generated references can support compact enhancement models.
  </details>

- **[CrossProjection: Benchmarking Spatial Grounding across Projection and Section Views](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.00473)**  `arXiv:2608.00473`  
  _Kaho Li, Zekai Lin, Pengyu Zeng, Yuqin Dai, Jun Yin, Tianjing Feng, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Plans, elevations, and sections describe a three-dimensional structure through incomplete projections that change how an entity is drawn, not only where it is seen from. Reading them means deciding which entities correspond across views and recovering where they lie. We introduce CrossProjection, a benchmark that uses architectural drawings to test whether vision-language models (VLMs) can turn correspondence decisions into geometric answers. Its tasks cover cross-view matching, projection registration, and novel-section prediction, with outputs ranging from judgments and candidate selection to free region boxes and directed section cuts. For inverse section localization, we introduce, to our knowledge, the first VLM benchmark protocol that accepts any cut within an expert-adjudicated band of compatible positions and checks the viewing direction separately. Manually annotated drawings and BIM-derived views provide 33,788 questions from 46 buildings, and we evaluate 22 VLMs on a common set of 2,763. Strong selection or reproduction does not imply cross-view localization: on 100 matched region targets, the best model redraws 98 marked boxes but localizes only 59 across views. Section cuts remain far from expert level, with the leading model trailing two architects by 51.9 and 67.4 percentage points on shared Natural and BIM line questions. Incorrect choices favor mirrored positions, and many cuts face the correct way but violate local geometry. Curriculum fine-tuning on BIM supervision teaches a 9B model to localize regions it could not localize before, raising box accuracy from 0% to 25.3% on held-out BIM buildings and from 0.3% to 30.8% on real drawing sets not used for fine-tuning, whereas section cuts remain largely out of reach.
  </details>

- **[OSEF: One-Step Evidence Fusion for Cross-Video Scene Procedure Planning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.29401)**  `arXiv:2607.29401`  
  _Zhentong Ye, Lei Zhang, Sijia Zhou, Yingda Yu, Yuehan Shi, Jiaqi Xuan, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Video Scene Procedure Planning (VSPP) predicts actions between supplied start and goal observations. We introduce Cross-Video Scene Procedure Planning (CVSPP), which instead takes a start-goal query and candidate videos, and predicts an action sequence together with its supporting video and interval. Two challenges arise: demonstrations of the same task can support different transitions, and an early retrieval error can deprive the planner of relevant evidence. We construct a dedicated benchmark from eleven video sources, with task-specific queries, candidate sets, and linked video-interval-plan references. Its fourteen settings support a broad study of nine adapted planner families. We propose One-Step Evidence Fusion (OSEF), which retains candidate features while producing interval-conditioned planning representations. Separate boundary scores model the supporting interval, and compatible-mass decoding combines the probability of the same complete plan across overlapping intervals before selecting the output. Joint evaluation requires video, interval, and plan to match one reference example. Across four matched development-data comparisons on NIV, CrossTask, and COIN, compatible-mass decoding increases mean joint success by 2.40-6.79 percentage points without retraining. On NIV, query-only controls retain plan accuracy yet sharply reduce joint success; donor-interface studies examine how VSPP models use retrieved visual states. We further identify temporal-reference sensitivity: changing only the reference projection can reverse the decoding gain, exposing an evaluation challenge for the new task.
  </details>

- **[MIBE: Multi-subject Interaction Benchmark and Evaluator for Personalized Image Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.01383)**  `arXiv:2607.01383`  
  _Zhihan Chen, Yuhuan Zhao, Yijie Zhu, Xinyu Yao, Mengcong Ren, Suwen Wang, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Multi-subject personalized image generation aims to compose multiple distinct reference identities into a coherent scene while preserving their prompt-specified interactions. Existing generators frequently exhibit subject-binding failures as scene complexity scales: omitting requested entities (Existence), blending visual attributes across subjects (Appearance), or misassigning actions and spatial relations (Interaction). Compounding this modeling bottleneck, existing evaluation metrics, which are designed primarily for single-subject similarity or holistic image preference, align only weakly with human judgment on these coupled errors, and several degrade toward random agreement as the number of interacting subjects increases. To address this evaluation gap, we introduce the Multi-subject Interaction Benchmark and Evaluator (MIBE), a unified framework pairing a factorized benchmark (MIB) with a reference-conditioned evaluator (MIE). MIB systematically varies subject count, human-/object-heavy composition, and relation type (non-contact, occlusion, and physical interaction) within a decoupled two-tier data regime: MIB-Silver, a 60K-pair training corpus annotated via a rubric-guided dual-VLM protocol, and MIB-Gold, a 4,020-pair evaluation suite annotated under a double-blind human protocol across six state-of-the-art generators spanning both seen and held-out unseen architectures. Trained exclusively on MIB-Silver with a dual-head objective that jointly predicts pairwise preference rankings and facet-level diagnostics, MIE achieves 0.922 overall pairwise agreement with human consensus on MIB-Gold, including 0.982 on seen generators and 0.884 on held-out unseen generators. Using MIBE for cross-generator diagnosis, we quantify systematic binding bottlenecks across modern generators, providing reproducible benchmark infrastructure and interpretable supervision for future model alignment.
  </details>

- **[PruneGround: Plug-and-play Spatial Pruning for 3D Visual Grounding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.31148)**  `arXiv:2606.31148`  
  _Duc Cao Dinh, Khai Le-Duc, Florent Draye, Chris Ngo, Terry Jingchen Zhang, Bernhard Schölkopf, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  3D Visual Grounding (3DVG) aims to localize target objects in 3D scenes given natural language descriptions. Existing approaches typically perform reasoning over the entire scene, leading to ambiguous predictions and high computational cost, especially in cluttered environments. We observe that many referential expressions rely on local spatial context and often correspond to restricted spatial regions rather than the full scene. Motivated by this insight, we propose PruneGround, an effective plug-and-play framework for 3DVG built upon three key components. First, we introduce Language-Guided Spatial Pruning (LGSP), which leverages a frozen Vision Language Model (VLM) to identify language-relevant regions, thereby reducing spatial computation and grounding candidates in the narrower search space. Second, we propose MultiView-Conditioned Description Reformulation (MCDR), which decomposes complex expressions into simplified target--anchor relations and augments missing spatial cues through multi-view reasoning. Finally, we propose LLM-Grounder, which repurposes a detection-pretrained spatial LLM into a language-conditioned grounding model by aligning point cloud and linguistic representations within the pruned region. Extensive experiments on the three most popular point cloud benchmarks demonstrate that our method achieves state-of-the-art results on all three ScanRefer settings and on 9 out of 10 Nr3D/Sr3D settings. Code and models are publicly available:this https URL
  </details>

- **[TempAct: Advancing Temporal Plausibility in Autoregressive Video Generation via Planner-Executor RL](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.28016)**  `arXiv:2606.28016`  
  _Jing Wang, Xiangxin Zhou, Jiajun Liang, Kaiqi Liu, Wanyuan Pang, Zhenyu Xie, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Autoregressive (AR) video diffusion models enable low-latency streaming generation by synthesizing videos chunk by chunk with cached visual context, but this chunk-wise formulation makes temporal instruction following ambiguous. A single global prompt does not specify which sub-event should be realized in each chunk, while naively switching to step-wise prompts often leads to delayed reactions, blended step semantics, and error propagation across prompt transitions. These failures are difficult to address with supervised fine-tuning or distillation alone: SFT suffers from exposure bias, while rollout-based distillation still optimizes low-level denoising or teacher-distribution matching rather than directly enforcing action ordering and prompt-transition correctness. We address these challenges with TempAct, a planner--executor reinforcement learning framework that jointly optimizes temporal decomposition and step-conditioned execution for temporally plausible AR video generation. TempAct uses an LLM planner to explore span-aware step prompts that are executable by the video model, and trains an AR diffusion executor to follow these prompts under its own generated histories. Its key mechanism is hierarchical group exploration: candidate plans form planning groups, and each plan induces an execution group of multiple continuations from a shared visual context, enabling plan-level credit assignment for long-horizon temporal outcomes and executor-level credit assignment for prompt-switch behavior. We further design hierarchical rewards that combine plan-quality and full-video temporal feedback for the planner with local transition-level step-following rewards, aesthetic regularization, and KL constraints for the executor. Experiments on Self-Forcing and LongLive show that TempAct improves temporal consistency while preserving overall visual quality.
  </details>

- **[Supervising Recurrent Vision Transformers from Bottlenecked Context](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.21562)**  `arXiv:2606.21562`  
  _Philippe Weinzaepfel, Christian Wolf, Mert Bülent Sariyildiz, Guillaume Bono, Gianluca Monaci_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Transformers are AI's workhorse but their computational cost becomes prohibitive when processing long sequences. We target long-horizon streaming vision and robotics applications, where it is particularly impractical to store and maintain a history of observations. Recurrent Transformers address this limitation by maintaining fixed-size memory but their performance lags behind that of transformers operating over the full observation history. We argue that this gap does not stem from architectural limitations, but from differences in how these models learn to compress past information. Without access to an observation history, recurrent models must explicitly decide what to retain in memory at each step, a significantly harder learning problem. In this work, we propose a distillation approach that transfers the compression strategy of a classical full-history transformer to a recurrent variant. We enable this by designing a teacher model that explicitly compresses its observation history into a fixed-size bottleneck representation and directly supervise the student's memory with this bottleneck representation, effectively aligning the two compression mechanisms. We show that this approach enables training of a recurrent latent robotic memory with linear-time complexity on the Mem-RPE task while substantially narrowing the performance gap to full-history transformers. We additionally validate the same principle on streaming visual question answering (VQA) and observe improved recurrent predictions thanks to memory distillation.
  </details>

- **[Attention Alignment Between Humans and Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.17410)**  `arXiv:2606.17410`  
  _Isaac R. Christian, Udith Haputhanthri, Declan Campbell, Samuel Nastase, Taylor Webb, Michael Graziano_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Visual perception depends on top-down goals and bottom-up sensory mechanisms. Vision-language models (VLMs) implement both, allowing us to treat each component as a separable hypothesis about what drives where we look. Following that logic, we trained four VLMs, crossing CNN and ViT encoders with LSTM and Transformer decoders in a 2$\times$2 factorial design. Our four models shared a training distribution, a vocabulary, a supervision signal, and every hyperparameter; only the encoder and decoder families differed. We extracted each model's attention weights on 200 images, for two separate tasks (social captioning and general description), and compared those weights to fixations from 49 participants performing the same tasks. We found that both decoder and encoder architecture shaped alignment, but decoder choice dominated. LSTM decoders reached 81-89% of the human upperbound and Transformer decoders 47-74%, with decoder architecture explaining nearly five times more variance in alignment than encoder architecture ($\eta^2 = 0.43$ vs. $0.09$). Despite their alignment advantage, LSTM-decoder attention maps were spatially diffuse and minimally task-differentiated; Transformer decoders, in contrast, were weaker in alignment yet showed sharper spatial concentration and stronger task differentiation. Attention weights also predicted fMRI signals from the Natural Scenes Dataset. Somewhat surprisingly, attention weights predicted early visual, ventral, and lateral cortex better than parietal cortex, a region often associated with the control of attention. And, unlike behavioral results in which decoder choice was most influential, encoder type contributed most to neural alignment, with the CNN driving the effect across decoder types. This dissociation suggests bottom-up and top-down VLM components make separable contributions to behavioral and neural attention alignment.
  </details>

- **[Pinpoint: Grounded Worldwide Image Geolocation via Cross-Source Retrieval and Reranking](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.04133)**  `arXiv:2606.04133`  
  _Nika Chuzhoy, Brian Hu, Amit A. Arora, Jae Ro, Sarthak S. Sahu_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Image geolocation aims to estimate where a photograph was taken from its visual content. At worldwide scale, this remains challenging because visual evidence is often ambiguous, diverse, and unevenly distributed. Prior work has typically treated geolocation of ordinary internet photos and street-view imagery as separate tasks, despite their complementary strengths: internet photos better match the appearance distribution of user-captured queries, while street-view imagery provides denser, geographically grounded coverage. We present Pinpoint, a retrieve-and-rerank architecture that combines both sources in a coarse-to-fine pipeline. A contrastive image-GPS embedder is trained on both user-uploaded Flickr photos and street-view imagery, learning a shared image-GPS embedding space that is used to retrieve candidate locations. An attention-based reranker then rescores retrieved candidates by combining candidate-level visual and GPS features with cross-source evidence from nearby locations to ground the prediction. Unlike recent prior work, Pinpoint does not rely on multimodal large-language models, making inference faster and more reproducible. Pinpoint achieves state-of-the-art results across all metrics on standard benchmarks for internet photos (IM2GPS3k and YFCC4k) and street-view imagery (OSV-5M).
  </details>

- **[How Far Has AI Come in Liver Fibrosis Staging? A Real-World Multi-Center Dataset and Benchmark](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.25595)**  `arXiv:2605.25595`  
  _Yuanye Liu, Nannan Shi, Zhejia Zhang, Hanxiao Zhang, Boya Wang, Derong Yu, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Despite years of methodological progress, how far AI has come in liver fibrosis staging has never been systematically evaluated under the heterogeneous, multi-center conditions that define clinical practice. To address this gap, we introduce LiFS, a multi-center dataset and benchmark derived from the MICCAI 2025 CARE-Liver challenge, comprising 610 patients across multiple centers and scanners with multi-sequence. To the best of our knowledge, LiFS is the first benchmark providing complete gadoxetic acid-enhanced sequences with histopathology-confirmed annotations from diverse real-world scanners. Through systematic evaluation of nine independently developed LiFS methods under a common CARE 2025 setting, and comparison with in-cohort radiologist, we assess how far current AI has progressed toward clinically meaningful liver fibrosis staging from three complementary perspectives. First, against radiologists, the best AI methods approached the performance of the senior radiologist in selected settings and exceeded the junior radiologist on selected endpoints while median AI performance generally approached junior-radiologist levels. Second, from a data perspective, cross-center heterogeneity, label imbalance, and contrast-enhanced sequence variability emerge as the dominant challenges for AI methods. In particular, the hepatobiliary phase offers valuable functional information but also introduces cross-center variability, creating a practical dilemma in its use. Third, from a technical perspective, controlled experiments quantify the effects of several factors, providing practical evidence for model design in liver fibrosis staging. Overall, LiFS provides a rigorous real-world benchmark for positioning the current state of AI in liver fibrosis staging and for enabling future research on the key challenges that limit clinically reliable deployment.
  </details>

- **[Distributed Image Compression with Multimodal Side Information at Extremely Low Bitrates](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22061)**  `arXiv:2605.22061`  
  _Guojun Xu, Mingyang Zhang, Jianwen Xiang, Cheng Tan, Yanchao Yang, Junwei Zhou_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Distributed Image Compression (DIC) is crucial for multi-view transmission, especially when operating at extremely low bitrates (< 0.1 bpp). Its core challenge is effectively utilizing side information to achieve high-quality reconstruction under strict bitrate budgets. However, existing DIC approaches struggle to exploit global context and object-level details from side information, leading to local blurring and the loss of fine details in the reconstruction. To address these limitations, we propose a Multimodal DIC framework (MDIC), which, for the first time, leverages side information in a multimodal manner into the DIC paradigm, effectively preserving fine-grained local details and enhancing global perceptual quality in reconstructed images. Specifically, we introduce a text-to-image diffusion-based decoder conditioned on textual side information extracted from correlated images to capture shared global semantics. Moreover, we design a feature-mask generator, supervised by a multimodal fine-grained alignment task, to strengthen the exploitation of visual side information. The generated mask serves two purposes: first, it guides the extraction of fine-grained details from losslessly transmitted side information to preserve the semantic consistency of reconstructed details; second, it regulates the extraction of clustered feature representations from the quantized VQ-VAE embeddings, compensating for category information lost under the extreme compression of the primary image. Extensive experiments on the widely used KITTI Stereo and Cityscapes datasets demonstrate that MDIC achieves state-of-the-art perceptual quality at extremely low bitrates.
  </details>

- **[OP2GS: Feature-Free Gaussian Splatting with Dual Opacity for 3D Instance Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.20044)**  `arXiv:2605.20044`  
  _Guiyu Liu, Niklas Vaara, Janne Mustaniemi, Juho Kannala, Janne Heikkilä_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) provides an explicit and efficient scene representation, but its primitives do not naturally expose object-level identity. Existing methods either learn contrastive per-Gaussian features that need post-hoc clustering, or supervise identity encodings with view-consistent 2D masks. We propose OP2GS, a lightweight object-aware Gaussian representation that augments each primitive with an explicit instance label and a dedicated instance opacity $\sigma^{*}$, which serves as an instance occupancy field for object-mask rendering. This dual-opacity formulation decouples visual appearance from instance occupancy, so that $\sigma^{*}$ can be learned and the instance labels can be corrected without touching the appearance parameters $\sigma$ and $c$. We learn $\sigma^{*}$ with an instance occupancy loss that follows the standard transmittance-based visibility of 3DGS. A discrete regrouping step then corrects the instance labels using multi-view mask consensus. Since no high-dimensional features are required, OP2GS can be plugged into existing 3DGS training pipelines and applied unchanged to frozen 3DGS assets. On the ScanNet++ validation set with the official class-agnostic protocol, OP2GS improves over OpenSplat3D, the strongest comparable baseline, with both SAM and EntitySeg masks; it is also best on Messy Rooms and, under the Gaga protocol, on Replica, while storing only one scalar and one integer per Gaussian. Code will be released.
  </details>

- **[CAB: Accelerating Flow and Diffusion Sampling via Rectification and Corrected Adams-Bashforth](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16736)**  `arXiv:2605.16736`  
  _Anuska Roy, Pravin Nair_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Flow and diffusion models achieve high-fidelity, high-resolution image synthesis, but often require many function evaluations (NFEs) at sampling time. Existing acceleration methods either require additional training through distillation or rely on training-free high-order solvers, and both can degrade sample quality at low NFE budgets. We propose CAB (Corrected Adams-Bashforth), a training-free sampler that accelerates both flow and diffusion models. CAB first transforms the sampling dynamics to a common rectified coordinate system, and then applies a multistep Adams-Bashforth predictor augmented with a simple correction term based on past velocity evaluations and therefore incurs no additional NFEs. The resulting method is simple, has the same algorithmic form across model classes, and has at least third-order local truncation error and second-order global error. Experiments on pretrained flow and diffusion models, including class-conditional and large-scale text-to-image benchmarks, show that CAB improves quality-NFE trade-offs in the low-step regime of 6-20 NFEs. It also remains competitive with strong training-free samplers at higher step counts across most tested models. The official implementation is available atthis https URL.
  </details>

- **[TANGO: Training-free Controllable Human Motion Generation with Progressive Token Guidance](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.14935)**  `arXiv:2605.14935`  
  _Nhat Le, Daochang Liu, Baoru Huang, Anh Nguyen, Ajmal Mian_
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  We present TANGO, a progressive token guidance framework for training-free controllable human motion generation. Unlike control approaches that primarily operate at a fixed temporal resolution, TANGO leverages a multi-scale hierarchy of discrete motion tokens to establish a structured control process, progressively guiding global motion structure before refining local details. At each scale, the differentiable control objective guides all current-scale token distributions, and the sampled tokens condition subsequent finer-scale predictions. To address the challenge of discrete categorical sampling, we adopt a first-order approach following the Bayesian principle, adjusting token sampling distributions with a single first-order update per scale. To further improve guidance consistency, we introduce Within-Scale Interdependency (WSI) guidance to account for how token choices jointly affect the control objective, and Cross-Scale Consistency (CSC) guidance to estimate how remaining finer scales may affect the final control outcome. Together, these complementary guidance mechanisms enable consistent and effective progressive control without additional control-specific training. Experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of TANGO across different control objectives in terms of motion quality, control accuracy, and generalization to unseen constraints.
  </details>

- **[BARISTA: A Multi-Task Egocentric Benchmark for Compositional Visual Understanding](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.12074)**  `arXiv:2605.12074`  
  _Patrick Knab, Orgest Xhelili, Inis Buzi, Drago Andres Guggiana Nilo, Mohd Saquib Khan, Lorenz Kolb, et al._
  <details><summary>Abstract</summary>
  Scene understanding is central to general physical intelligence, and video is a primary modality for capturing both state and temporal dynamics of a scene. Yet understanding physical processes remains difficult, as models must combine object localization, hand-object interactions, relational parsing, temporal reasoning, and step-level procedural inference. Existing benchmarks usually evaluate these capabilities separately, limiting diagnosis of why models fail on procedural tasks. We introduce BARISTA, a densely annotated egocentric dataset and benchmark of 185 real-world coffee-preparation videos covering fully automatic, portafilter-based, and capsule-based workflows. BARISTA provides verified per-frame scene graphs linking persistent object identities to masks, tracks, boxes, attributes, typed relations, hand-object interactions, activities, and process steps.
